correctness.rationale: The source proves that one iteration preserves the first homology group and appends the reduced denominator \(P_kH+1\). Therefore \(H\) stays fixed, \(P_{k+1}=P_k(P_kH+1)\), and \(Q_k=HP_k\) satisfies \(Q_{k+1}=Q_k(Q_k+1)\). The exact product identity gives \(d_{k+1}=1+Q_0\prod_{j=1}^k d_j\), so later orders are \(1\) modulo every earlier order and modulo every prime divisor of \(Q_0\). The growth bound follows by iterating \(Q_{k+1}>Q_k^2\). No finite computation is used as proof.
